title: Farmers protest in Davangere against Bhadra canal water release

tea.why: Farmers oppose the state government's order to release additional water from the Bhadra Reservoir to Chitradurga district during a drought.
tea.want: Withdrawal of the water release order and a meeting of the Irrigation Consultative Committee before any further water distribution decisions.
tea.changed: Nov 2: Minister S S Mallikarjun announced the water release is on hold following discussions with the Chief Minister and protesting farmers.

summary: Farmers from the Bhadra command area in Karnataka staged a protest outside the residence of District In-charge Minister S S Mallikarjun in Davangere on November 2, 2026. The demonstrators, representing several taluks, opposed the state government's decision to release an additional one tmc ft of water from the Bhadra Reservoir to the Upper Bhadra canal for Chitradurga district. Protesters argued the move was made without consulting the Irrigation Consultative Committee and would negatively impact local farmers during drought conditions. Minister S S Mallikarjun met with the protesters and subsequently announced that the water release had been paused. Following an assurance from Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, the farmers temporarily called off their agitation, pending further discussions with the government.
demands: Withdrawal of the water release order
Convening of the Irrigation Consultative Committee
Continuous water supply for 120 days for summer crops
response: Minister S S Mallikarjun stated he opposed the release and had communicated this to the Water Resources Minister. The Chief Minister has invited a farmer delegation for further discussions.

updates.text: Farmers gathered near Shamanur overbridge and marched to the minister's residence to protest the water release order.
Minister S S Mallikarjun announced the water release is on hold and the protest was called off following an assurance from the Chief Minister.
